declarations.name: find
declarations.description: Fuzzy filename/directory path lookup; returns paths only. Only when the target path is unknown and cannot be directly resolved but a fragment is known; general discovery: glob.

query.description: Filename/path fragment; space-separated fragments AND-match within one path.

path.description: Base directory; omit for the current Project.

declarations.name: glob
declarations.description: Wildcard file-path lookup under a known directory; directories never match. No preliminary listing. Unknown base: find first with a known path fragment.

pattern.description: Union of patterns under one base; separate calls for other bases or per-pattern results.

path.description: Known existing base directory; omit for the current Project.

sort.description: mtime default (newest first); natural = raw walk order, cheaper on huge trees.

declarations.name: grep
declarations.description: Search literal/regex file contents (single-line ripgrep); returns path:line blocks with context, patch-ready. Broad reconnaissance: mode:files; locating: context:0; every pattern and scope in one call, and the anchors are the windows for one read. Symbol relations: code_graph.

path.description: Plain file/directory scopes; omit for Project root. Every pattern searches every path; pattern/path pairs need separate calls.

glob.description: Relative glob filter evaluated inside path, e.g. "*.cs" or "src/**/*.ts"; for exact/absolute paths use path instead.

mode.description: content default; files lists matching paths; count totals all patterns together per file.

limit.description: Requested results; default 250; 0 unlimited. Context output caps at 40 blocks; continue via the returned offset.

context.description: Omit for automatic context; 0 for matches only.

text.description: Search binary data as text (archives/Git objects not decoded).

declarations.name: read
declarations.description: Read file windows or images. One call per read stage: {file_path, offset, limit} entries for every located site, never a whole large file. Content in context is never read again. Missing paths are reported, never replaced. Directories: list. Binaries: bounded hex. Rows carry no line numbers; `[lines a-b]` gives each block's range. Never count rows: before writing a line number, copy it from grep, code_graph or git diff output; otherwise cite path and symbol.

file_path.description: Overlapping windows of one file merge. A glob fans out to ≤10 newest files.

limit.description: Maximum line count; default 500 per exact file, 25 per glob-expanded file; batch default. Lines only: PDFs use pages.

pages.description: PDF page range "N" or "N-M", 1-based, ≤20 pages per call. Text pages return text; scanned pages (no text layer) return page images, or OCR text on a text-only model. Without pages, a PDF over 10 pages returns its first 5 pages and page count.

declarations.name: code_graph
declarations.description: Code structure and relations from the parsed graph, no text matching. symbols → file outline rows `[export ]kind name (Lstart-end) signature`; find_symbol returns declaration/body; references adds usages; callers/callees return locations; dependents/impact → importers and blast radius. Exact identifiers: find_symbol/references/callers/callees; keywords: symbol_search/search; literal text and regex belong to grep. Prefer it over read/grep for declarations and relations. symbols already outlines a file: never pair it with overview for one need.

mode.description: File modes (files[]): overview, imports, dependents, related, impact. symbols with files[] gives the file outline; other modes use symbols[].

files.description: Paths, project-relative or absolute; required for file modes, symbol queries span all files.

symbols.description: Exact identifiers/keywords; required for symbol modes, optional outline filter. Every symbol searches every file; distinct pairs need separate calls.

body.description: true for implementation, false for locations; find_symbol defaults true, references is opt-in.

limit.description: Max results; modes may cap lower.

depth.description: Overview hierarchy or caller traversal depth; default 1.

cwd.description: Explicit root outside the project; omit for project root.

declarations.name: git
declarations.description: Run Git here, never through shell. An array runs in order and stops on failure; batch read-only commands in one. diff for known changes, status to discover them; history only when needed. git diff or git diff -- <paths> includes untracked files. Set include_stage_ids:true to select changes, then action:stage with diff_id/change_ids. Staging rejects stale or cross-Project diffs and returns per-file staged counts. Worktrees are managed only: action:worktree; git worktree add/remove/list/prune map to managed operations (add -b keeps the session in place; add --detach makes a read-only snapshot worktree, removed when its turn ends, and is the one add a delegated worker may run; list --porcelain stays raw git; move/lock/unlock/repair are refused). Merge or remove only when the user asks.

action.description: Default command. stage uses diff_id/change_ids instead of command. worktree uses worktree_action and its fields.

command.description: Full commands starting with git; shell-style quoting, no pipes/redirects/substitution (a && chain runs as the array). Mutations allowed.

output_limit.description: Body line cap; staging IDs are not capped. Default 500; git log defaults to 100. A cut ends with [output capped …] naming how to continue.

include_stage_ids.description: Include staging IDs outside the body cap for git diff or git diff -- <paths> only. Default false.

diff_id.description: stage: exact diff_id from git diff.

change_ids.description: stage: exact change ID or IDs to stage, including new files.

worktree_action.description: enter: create or re-enter the managed worktree (branch: that branch, create: new); return: back to the project folder, worktree kept; merge: into its merge target; remove; list; prune.

session_id.description: enter/return/merge/remove: another session (it must be idle); default the caller.

branch.description: enter: use the worktree of this branch instead. remove: this session's worktree of that branch.

create.description: enter with branch: create that branch.

carry.description: enter: the user answer to WORKTREE_DIRTY_CHOICE (uncommitted project-folder changes).

confirm_large.description: enter or git worktree add: the user accepted the WORKTREE_LARGE_REPO_CONFIRM size.

force.description: remove: discard dirty/unmerged work; only on explicit user request.

declarations.name: load_tool
declarations.description: Load full schemas for missing deferred tool names/aliases; a connector name loads all its tools; batch needed names in one call.

declarations.name: computer
declarations.description: Operate local desktop apps (Windows, macOS, Linux), OS dialogs, and user-viewed or handed-over browser tabs (no Browser Use trial). Only for steps no built-in, mcp__* (deferred too), shell/CLI, or Browser Use tool covers; never a stand-in for a page action browser refused. Load the computer-use skill before first use. At most one computer call per model turn; other tools may run in the same turn. Chain same-window steps inside one act. Every window action names one exact target (window_id, or app resolving to one window); zoom instead inherits its target from frame_id. Input requires a fresh observation from capture or the previous result. Refs, marks, and frames come only from the latest observation of that window (refs 5 min, frames/marks 60 s; invalidated by UI mutation); an automatic post-action observation replaces the old state. Never guess ids. Observation-only actions, safe to repeat: list, diagnose, capture, verify, wait_for_user. Every other action can move the desktop.

parametersJsonSchema.description: One compact Computer Use operation. Use act.actions to execute 1-6 simple actions and receive one fresh observation.

action.description: Use capture to observe, act for simple input actions, and the remaining operations only for their named advanced capability.

timeout_ms.description: Wait for manual or host-configured idle resume; default 60000.

kind.description: history returns this session's own executed commands with their verdicts, for reviewing what a run already did.

query.description: With kind="apps", also lists installed apps whose name or id matches, including apps that are not running.

limit.description: kind="history" only: how many of the most recent records to return; default 60.

window_id.description: Exact id from list(kind="windows"), e.g. hwnd:0x123ABC.

ocr_language.description: Optional OS OCR language tag to verify, e.g. ko or en-US.

app.description: App name used only when it resolves to one exact window.

screen.description: Display index for a plain vision capture.

mode.description: state (default) is structured UI plus image; som adds marks; vision is image only; ax is accessibility only. zoom uses frame_id and region only; omit window_id, app and screen. Each element is one line: #mark [ref] Role "name", then value=, state=, source= (non-UIA), disabled and focused only when they apply, @x,y,width,height and its actions. OCR text reads "text" @x,y,width,height line=N.

frame_id.description: Latest unexpired frame id; required with mode="zoom" and supplies its exact target window.

include_ocr.description: State/SOM automatically use offline OS OCR when semantic targets are absent; true always runs OCR even when semantic targets exist. OCR shares max_elements. Zoom recognizes the crop itself, which is how enlarged text becomes readable.

image_output.description: inline (default) returns the frame here; file writes it beside the run and returns its path.

role.description: Control type filter, e.g. Button, Edit.

include_noninteractive.description: Also static text, panes, groups; default false.

max_elements.description: Total returned accessibility + OCR element budget. state defaults to 80.

continuation.description: Next-page token from a capture cut at max_elements.

items.description: One action; act.actions defines ordering and target reuse.

x.description: Frame-relative X; act.input.frame_id owns the frame.

y.description: Frame-relative Y; act.input.frame_id owns the frame.

waypoints.description: Drag points in act.input.frame_id for a gesture that is not a straight line; replaces x/y and to_x/to_y.

modifiers.description: Optional pointer modifiers joined by +. Background supports ctrl/shift; alt requires foreground delivery.

text.description: Literal text; foreground cap 4000 UTF-16 code units per action. Never a password, or a code from SMS, an authenticator app or a passkey, even one shown on screen: saved_login or handoff_user. The one exception is a one-time code e-mailed for a sign-up or sign-in you started, read from a connected mailbox: type it yourself, never echo it.

value.description: set_value replacement for an element that advertises set_value; writes the control directly, without focus or keystrokes. Never a password or a code; an e-mailed code is typed with text and delivery foreground (set_value fills only one box of a segmented code input).

keys.description: Key name or chord. Keyboard chords with ctrl/shift/alt require explicit foreground delivery; background supports plain keys.

duration.description: wait: cap in seconds. act already settles after every action; use wait only for a known async delay.

quiet.description: wait: opt-in (default false, a fixed pause). true ends before duration once the window set, foreground, focused window, title and bounds stop changing (3 equal samples 200 ms apart); use it when waiting for a window or dialog to open, close or move. Content changes inside a window (canvas, text) are not seen: use verify for those.

actions.description: First: an input action. Then type/key/wait reusing focus, or click/double_click/triple_click/scroll/set_value/type/key on a ref from the same observation (no marks or coordinates). act already settles after each action; wait is a fixed pause for a known async delay (quiet:true ends it early once windows stop changing; see wait.quiet) and totals ≤10s; use verify for a real condition. Transition/failure or a changed, disabled, or off-screen ref stops the rest.

observe.description: Returned observation. Default: ax when the first action targets a ref (full state if the tree is unusable), otherwise state. state includes the frame for coordinates or visual checks; ax skips the screenshot. A repeat observation of the same window may send elements_delta instead of elements: unchanged lists "old ref=live ref" ranges for rows that look identical to the list you hold (s1:e0..e4=s9:e0..e4), added has every other row in full, removed the old refs that are gone. Every ref from an earlier observation is retired: act only with the live ref on the right of "=" or on an added row. A new window, a dialog or a large change returns the full elements list, and capture always does.

delivery.description: Background by default for supported semantic/message input. Use explicit foreground for unsupported routes, real pointer/focus requirements, or demonstrations. Never replay uncertain input in another mode.

confirm.description: terminate only, and required for it: kills the process behind the window, losing unsaved work. Ask the user first.

x.description: move only: new left edge; y the top; width/height an optional new size.

path.description: Exact labels from the bar down, e.g. ["File","Save As"]. Missing, ambiguous, or disabled entries fail closed.

expect.description: AND-combined predicates. Reads state only: no pixels, and prior refs stay valid.

present.description: Text an element name or value must contain.

savedAccount.description: Fallback sign-in in the user's own browser; prefer its existing session/SSO or Browser Use's saved sign-in. Saved login (username or masked label; a miss lists the site's labels) written after host checks into the focused field of a Chrome/Edge HTTPS page. The site receives it. A password is kept from you and its browser's pixels are withheld this turn, but a page that redisplays it can expose it, and other programs of the same Windows user are outside this protection; a username is not hidden. On refusal hand the secret to the user (handoff_user secret, surface computer).

field.description: username (text field) or password (password field). Codes from SMS or an authenticator app, passkeys, security keys and app approvals are the user's step: handoff_user takeover. An e-mailed code you can read from a connected mailbox is yours: type it.

input.description: Fields for the selected action. Allowed input by action (* required): wait_for_user(timeout_ms>=0<=120000); list(kind*,query,limit); diagnose(window_id,ocr_language); capture(window_id,app,screen,mode,frame_id,region,include_ocr,ocr_language,image_output,query,role,visible_only,include_noninteractive,max_elements,continuation); act(window_id,app,frame_id,actions*,observe,delivery); window(window_id,app,operation*=focus|move|minimize|maximize|restore|close|terminate,confirm,x,y,width,height); menu(window_id,app,path*); verify(window_id,app,expect*,timeout_ms>=0<=30000,stable_samples); clipboard(operation*=read|write,text); launch(app*); saved_login(window_id,app,savedAccount*,field*).
